guardrails: Never advance running before surgeon clearance at week 6 imaging
10% weekly mileage rule — hard cap, same as ultra-plan-generator
Jaw pain during or after activity = stop and contact surgeon, not a "push through it" signal
Jaw clenching under heavy loads risks hardware displacement — no maximal-effort lifts until month 6+
Vert lags mileage by 2–4 weeks during rebuild
Feeling good is a yellow flag, not permission to add volume
Aerobic fitness recovers faster than tissue — don't let fitness metrics drive pacing of volume
No makeup miles after missed or reduced weeks

phases.label: Pre-op
notes: Maintain current volume (50+ mpw), no new peak attempts
Full strength routine, emphasize posterior chain and lower body — upper body goes offline first post-op
Avoid exercises that cause jaw clenching (heavy deadlifts, max squats) close to surgery
Begin protein-loading awareness
Stock liquid/soft food supplies

phases.label: Phase 1 — Survival

weeks.crossTrain: None — short gentle walks only (5–10 min)

notes: No elevated heart rate — blood pressure and bleeding risk
Sleep elevated, ice protocol per surgeon
Liquid diet only — protein shakes, smoothies, broth
This is survival, not training

phases.label: Phase 2 — Walking

weeks.crossTrain: Easy walks 15–20 min, flat only, conversational effort

weeks.strength: None (upper body waits until week 6–8 min.; lower body until 8–12; core until 8–10)
weeks.crossTrain: Brisk walks up to 30–40 min; elliptical or stationary bike only if surgeon approves

notes: Week 6 milestone: post-op imaging confirms bone position — first clearance gate
Do not advance to Phase 3 without surgeon sign-off at week 6
Reason for strength delay: jaw clenching under load risks hardware displacement and non-union

phases.label: Phase 3 — Foundation rebuild

weeks.running: None unless cleared early — wait for explicit surgeon clearance
weeks.strength: Nothing yet — bodyweight lower body starts week 8

weeks.running: Walk/jog intervals: 1 min jog / 2 min walk × 6–8 reps, 1–2 miles max, flat only
weeks.strength: Bodyweight lower body (squats, lunges, step-ups, hip hinges)
weeks.crossTrain: Rowing optional from week 10+: easy 20–30 min Z2, only if breathing feels clear

weeks.running: Easy jogging 2–3 miles, conversational pace only
weeks.strength: Light lower body loading (goblet squats, RDLs — nothing that causes jaw clench)
weeks.crossTrain: Rowing optional: easy 20–30 min Z2, stop if jaw pressure or elevated HR

weeks.running: Easy running 3–5 miles, 3x/week, no hills, no effort — pure aerobic
weeks.strength: Gradual return to trap bar deadlifts and back squats at submaximal loads

weeks.running: Easy running 4–6 miles, building to 3–4x/week, first vert introduction at walk pace
weeks.strength: Trap bar deadlifts/back squats continue at submaximal loads; upper body loading if surgeon clears jaw loading

notes: Red flags — stop and call surgeon: jaw pain during or after running, increased swelling post-activity, hardware sensation change, difficulty breathing through nose during effort

phases.label: Phase 4 — Volume build

weeklyTemplate.focus: Group run — start 4–5 mi, build toward 6–8 mi
Quality — hills before tempo, vert introduced carefully
Long run — start 8 mi, build toward pre-surgery long-run distance

stats.label: Vert
stats.value: Lags mileage by 2–4 weeks; needs ≥3 stable weeks at a mileage level first

stats.label: Strength
stats.value: Full compound lifts by week 20–24 if upper body cleared

notes: Heavy jaw-clenching sets postponed to month 6+
PT micro-dose circuits resume Mon/Wed/Fri as running returns
Feeling good is not permission to add volume

phases.label: Phase 5 — Return to performance

timeline.detail: 6–8 months post-op (only with zero complications and strong tissue response)

benchmarks: 8+ weeks of consistent 30–35 mpw with no setbacks
Vert tolerance confirmed through progressive hill introduction
No jaw-related symptoms during or after training
notes: Full training cycle possible — treated like re-entering a plan from scratch
If a race goal exists, transition to the ultra-plan-generator skill for a periodized block

nutrition.label: Liquid / soft diet (weeks 1–6+)
notes: Protein shakes, smoothies, broth, yogurt, soft foods
Target 1.6–2.0g protein/kg bodyweight to minimize muscle loss
Expect 5–10 lb weight loss and muscle loss — this is unavoidable, don't try to train through it

nutrition.label: Transition diet
notes: Soft solid foods as surgeon permits
Resume normal fueling as running returns
Long runs: resume carb + sodium fueling (70–80g carbs/hr) once runs exceed 60 min

nutrition.label: Full performance nutrition
notes: Full return to race-day fueling protocol — gels, salt capsules, hydration mix as before
